saints.name: St. John of Sahagún
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: An Augustinian friar and fearless preacher who made peace in the feuding city of Salamanca…
biography: Born at Sahagún in the kingdom of León in 1419, John González de Castrillo was educated by the Benedictines of his native town and then by Alfonso de Cartagena, bishop of Burgos, who ordained him priest in 1445 and made him a canon of his cathedral. Scrupulous over the holding of many benefices, John resigned all but one poor chaplaincy and went to Salamanca to study theology.

A grave illness there moved him to vow the religious life; in 1463 he entered the Hermits of St. Augustine, making profession the next year, and rose to be master of novices and, in 1471, prior. Devoted above all to the Eucharist, he became the most powerful preacher in that university city.

He scourged without fear the feuds of Salamanca's noble factions and the vices of the great, and his preaching reconciled the blood-divided city, which honours him as its patron. He died on 11 June 1479 — later lives say poisoned by a woman whose paramour he had converted — and Alexander VIII canonized him in 1690.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 12 June
